summary: A first-person excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 14, part 133) in which the narrator, after disabling a sleeping man named Simon, searches his apartment. She has stowed herself in a room, grabbed a knife, copied his stored videos and photos to her computer via his iPhone, and is now trying passcodes on a second phone she found in his pocket. The tense, claustrophobic scene is built around fear, waiting, and quick decisions.
one_line: A tense fiction excerpt where the narrator, alone with a drugged or unconscious Simon, copies data from his phones.
key_facts: The narrator switched off her camera and looked for a weapon, considering a can of Axe spray and a shard from the spotty mirror over the sink.
The narrator found a knife beside the sink and held it along with the can of Axe spray as she went to the bedroom.
Simon was curled up on the bed and did not move when the narrator nudged him with the toe of her boot, which felt like poking a sandbag.
The narrator unbolted the door, grabbed her bag and coat, and stood outside on the porch still holding the knife.
Simon's iPhone was sticking out of his back pocket, and the narrator drew it out with her finger and thumb.
The narrator plugged Simon's iPhone into her computer using its USB cable and logged in with his passcode.
The narrator dragged all of Simon's stored videos and photos to her desktop but could not copy his message files or contacts.
The narrator remembered that Katie lives next to the Semper Opera House.
Simon had slid a second phone into his right pocket, the side he was lying on.
The narrator rolled Simon onto his back, and he groaned and then started to snore.
When the narrator powered on the second phone, it asked for a password.
The narrator tried the passcodes "njme" and "simonisgr8" without success.
